function: Radar-based user identification (pp. 2, 4): a DNN picks which radar-detected object is the communication user; it designs no beam, waveform, or resource. Reason: function.
notes: Excluded at Step 1 with code function, the first that applies. The learned DNN solves radar-to-communication user identification, which is not the problem of any of the seven areas. p. 2: "we aim to determine the communication target within the radar measurement"; "given the beam index, we aim to find the communication user within the radar targets". p. 4: "This network then returns the likelihood of the candidate object being the communication target". p. 5: "In Table I, we show the accuracy of detecting the target object among the candidates" (DNN 0.9343). The beam is an input of the DNN, not its output: p. 2: "the optimal solution can be obtained by an exhaustive search over the beams of the codebook"; p. 4: "the beam providing the most power and the corresponding power level is saved as the optimal beamforming vector". So it is neither area 5 (no beam, waveform, or resource serving sensing and communication is designed; ISAC and beam training are only the motivation, p. 1) nor area 3; the task is closest to the excluded target or emitter identification. Earlier codes do not apply: a research letter that proposes and evaluates a method, with a learned DNN (p. 1: "we develop a robust and scalable deep neural network (DNN) solution"); not above_phy, because this user identification associates radar detections with the beam of the link on physical-layer measurements and is not the cell user association of that list (reviewer to confirm). Later codes would not apply either: MISO link (p. 1: "we consider a MISO channel with N element antenna array at the basestation") and quantitative results (Table I, p. 5). Identity check: the PDF is arXiv:2411.06578v1 (p. 1), whose title and authors (Demirhan, Alkhateeb) match the Crossref record of this DOI (IEEE Wireless Communications Letters 14(9), 2698-2702, 2025).
